sections.title: Engineering practices and on-call
sections.tags: on-call, pagerduty, code review, pull request, deploy, release, incident, postmortem, sev1, feature flags, engineering, testing, ci, on-call pay, rotation, weekend on call
sections.body:
Code review: every change is reviewed by at least one other engineer. Aim to review within 1 business day. Reviews are kind and specific. Comment on the code, never the person.
Branching and releases: trunk-based development with short-lived branches. We release to production twice a week (Tuesday and Thursday). Risky changes go behind a feature flag. No production deploys on Fridays or before holidays unless it is a fix for an incident.
Testing: changes need automated tests. CI must pass before merging.
RFCs: significant design changes need an RFC (see Decision-making and planning).

On-call: engineers on production-facing squads join a weekly rotation after their first 90 days.
- Shifts run Wednesday 10:00am to the following Wednesday 10:00am, primary and secondary.
- Pay: an on-call stipend of $300 per week for primary and $150 per week for secondary.
- If you are paged outside working hours for more than 30 minutes, you may take comp time the next day. Tell your manager.
- Swaps: trade shifts with a teammate and update PagerDuty. You do not need approval.
- Holidays: holiday on-call pays double the stipend.

Incident severity:
- Sev 1: customer-impacting outage or data risk. Page immediately, an incident commander is named, updates every 30 minutes.
- Sev 2: a major feature is degraded. Respond within 1 hour.
- Sev 3: minor issue with a workaround. Handle in business hours.
- Sev 4: cosmetic or low-impact. Add to backlog.
Postmortems: every Sev 1 and Sev 2 gets a blameless postmortem within 5 business days. We look at the system, not at who made a mistake.
Security issues found in code or infrastructure go to security@meridianworks.example straight away.

sections.title: Sales process and deal desk
sections.tags: sales process, pipeline stages, discount, deal desk, pricing approval, forecast, salesforce, opportunity, proposal, order form, quote, negotiation, close plan, security questionnaire
sections.body:
Pipeline stages in Salesforce, with the exit criteria to move forward:
1. Qualify: the prospect has a named problem, a budget holder is identified, and there is a reason to act within 6 months.
2. Discovery: we understand their facilities, systems and the cost of the problem in their own numbers.
3. Demo: a tailored demo on their data or sandbox data, with at least two decision makers present.
4. Pilot or proof: a time-boxed trial (usually 30 days) with written success criteria agreed in advance.
5. Proposal: a written order form with pricing, scope and term.
6. Negotiation: legal and security review in progress, with a mutual close plan.
7. Closed won or lost: record the reason within 24 hours.

Discounts: list prices are in the Sales space. Discounts need approval before you commit to them in writing. Up to 10% off list: the AE can approve. 10% to 20%: Sales Director. 20% to 30%: VP of Sales. Over 30%, or any multi-year deal with a price lock: VP of Sales and CFO. Deal desk (#deal-desk) turns requests around in 1 business day. Never offer a discount, free module or custom term in an email before it is approved.
Contracts: customers may use our standard order form or their own paper. Anything other than the standard goes to Legal through #legal-requests. Only officers can sign. You cannot sign for the company.
Security questionnaires: send them to #security-reviews, never fill them in on your own. Sales Engineering and Security answer them, normally within 5 business days.
Forecasting: update your opportunities by Thursday 5:00pm. The weekly forecast call is on Fridays. Forecast categories are Commit, Best Case and Pipeline, and Commit deals need a signed or near-final order form.
CRM rules: every opportunity needs a next step and a close date. See Onboarding for Sales.

sections.title: Customer Success playbook
sections.tags: customer success, csm, onboarding customers, health score, qbr, renewals, churn, expansion, go-live, escalation, customer health, account management
sections.body:
Customer journey and our targets:
- Kickoff: within 5 business days of signature. The CSM and an implementation engineer meet the customer's project team.
- Integration: connect the customer's systems through Connect. Target: 3 weeks (currently 6).
- Go-live: users are trained and data is flowing. Target: 60 days from signature.
- First value: the first measured bottleneck and a recommended fix. Target: 30 days from go-live.
- Business reviews: a QBR every quarter for customers above $50,000 in annual value, and twice a year for others.
- Renewal: starts 120 days before the renewal date.

Customer health score (0 to 100), recalculated weekly from: product usage (40%), support experience (20%), executive engagement (20%), and outcomes achieved (20%). Red is below 50, yellow 50 to 75, green above 75. A red account needs a written recovery plan within 5 business days, reviewed with your manager.
QBR agenda: results since last time, goals for next quarter, product roadmap highlights, open issues. Send the agenda 3 days ahead and the notes within 24 hours.
Renewal timeline: T-120 days: check health and stakeholder map. T-90: share value summary and proposed terms. T-60: pricing and legal review. T-30: signed or an escalation plan. No renewal is left to auto-renew without a conversation.
Expansion: spot opportunities from usage (new facilities, more modules) and pass them to the account's AE. You are credited through the expansion plan.
Escalations: if a customer threatens to cancel or asks for an executive, tell your manager and the VP of Customer Success within 1 business day.

sections.title: Support playbook and escalation
sections.tags: support, tickets, zendesk, escalation, macros, csat, status page, customer communication, first response, p1, p2, handoff, support team, how to handle a ticket
sections.body:
Handling a ticket:
1. Read the whole thread and the account history before replying.
2. Acknowledge the problem in the first sentence, and give a specific next step with a time.
3. Reproduce the issue in the sandbox if you can.
4. Resolve it, or escalate with the information engineering needs.
5. Confirm with the customer before closing, and record the cause.

Response targets are in the Support SLA table on the Data tab: P1 15 minutes (24/7), P2 1 hour, P3 8 business hours, P4 2 business days.
Escalation to engineering: use the "Escalate" form in the support tool. Include the account, steps to reproduce, expected and actual results, logs or screenshots, and business impact. For P1 and P2, also page the on-call engineer through PagerDuty. Never DM an engineer directly for a customer-impacting issue.
During an incident: the incident commander owns customer communication. Support posts updates on the status page every 30 minutes for Sev 1 and every hour for Sev 2. Use approved wording only.
Macros: saved replies are a starting point, never a finished reply. Personalize them. Never paste a macro without reading it.
What not to say: do not promise dates for fixes or features that are not approved, do not blame the customer, and do not share another customer's information.
Quality: our CSAT target is 4.6 out of 5 and first-contact resolution target is 70%. Managers review a sample of tickets with each person every two weeks.
Tough customers: stay calm and factual. If a customer is abusive, you may end the call politely and tell your team lead. Nobody has to tolerate abuse.
Holiday coverage: support keeps P1 and P2 coverage on company holidays. Covering staff get a day off in lieu within 30 days.

sections.title: Engineering tech stack and architecture
sections.tags: tech stack, architecture, aws, kubernetes, postgres, kafka, typescript, python, go, services, infrastructure, databases, monitoring, engineering overview, microservices, data pipeline
sections.body:
Overview: Meridian Flow is a multi-tenant cloud application. Customer systems send events (shipments, orders, dock appointments, machine status) through Connect into our pipeline. We build a live model of each facility, run detection on it, and show results in the web app and through alerts.

Main pieces:
- Web app: TypeScript and React, served from a Node backend-for-frontend.
- Services: mostly Go for the event pipeline and scheduling, and Python for the detection models in Bottleneck Radar.
- Data: PostgreSQL for customer configuration and state, Kafka for events, and a columnar store for history and analytics. Object storage holds raw uploads.
- Infrastructure: AWS (two regions, with a separate EU region for European customers), Kubernetes, and Terraform for everything as code.
- Integrations: Connect has prebuilt connectors for common ERP, TMS and WMS systems, plus a public REST API and webhooks. Each connector has an owner.
- Observability: Datadog for metrics, logs and traces. PagerDuty for paging. Every service has a dashboard and an on-call runbook.
- Security: single sign-on for customers, role-based access, encryption at rest and in transit, and per-tenant data isolation.

Repos and ownership: the monorepo holds the web app and most services. Each directory has an owner listed in CODEOWNERS, which decides who reviews a change. Squads own services end to end, including on-call.
Environments: local, staging and production. Staging uses synthetic customer data only. Never copy production data to staging or your laptop.
Where to learn more: the architecture overview and service catalog are in Notion under Engineering. The #eng-help channel is the place for questions.

sections.title: Setting up your development environment
sections.tags: dev setup, development environment, local build, install, clone repo, docker, makefile, github access, troubleshooting, first build, ide, run tests, setup guide, onboarding engineers
sections.body:
Goal: a working local build by the end of day 2. If you are stuck after 2 hours, ask in #eng-help. Do not struggle alone.

Steps:
1. Get access: request GitHub, AWS (read-only) and Datadog through Okta. Your manager approves.
2. Install the tools: Homebrew, Git, Docker Desktop, Node (use the version in .nvmrc), Go and Python (versions in the repo's tool-versions file). IT pre-installs some of these on your laptop.
3. Clone the monorepo with SSH. Set up your SSH key in GitHub and enable single sign-on for it.
4. Run the bootstrap script from the repo root. It installs dependencies, starts local services in Docker, and loads synthetic sample data.
5. Run the test suite for the service you will work on. A passing run confirms your setup.
6. Start the app locally and open it in the browser. Log in with the seeded test account.
7. Install the pre-commit hooks. They run formatting and basic security checks before each commit.

Common problems:
- Docker out of memory: give Docker at least 8 GB in its settings.
- Port already in use: stop other local services, or change the port in your local config.
- Tests fail with a database error: re-run the bootstrap script to recreate the local database.
- Permission denied pulling a package: your GitHub single sign-on is not authorized. Authorize it in GitHub settings.
Rules: never commit secrets, never use production credentials on your laptop, and never load customer data locally. Synthetic data only.
First pull request: see Onboarding for Engineering. Pair with a teammate for your first one.

sections.title: Incident commander guide
sections.tags: incident commander, incident response, sev1, outage, war room, status page, comms lead, after action, runbook, incident roles, major incident, escalation engineering
sections.body:
When a Sev 1 or major Sev 2 incident is declared, the on-call engineer names an incident commander (IC). The IC can be anyone trained. Being IC is not about fixing the problem. It is about coordinating.

Roles:
- Incident commander: owns the incident, decides, and assigns tasks. Does not debug.
- Technical lead: directs the investigation and the fix.
- Communications lead: updates the status page and internal channels, and supports the customer-facing teams. Usually from Support or Customer Success.
- Scribe: records a timeline in the incident doc.

First 15 minutes:
1. Declare the incident in #incidents with a short description and severity.
2. Open a video bridge and an incident doc from the template.
3. Name the roles aloud.
4. Post the first status update within 15 minutes of declaration.
5. Decide what is the impact and who is affected.

Updates: every 30 minutes for Sev 1 and every hour for Sev 2, even if the update is "no change". Post updates in #incidents and on the status page (using the approved wording).
Stop the harm first: restoring service comes before finding the root cause. Roll back if that is the fastest way.
Closing: the IC declares the incident resolved when the customer impact has ended and monitoring confirms it. Customers are told.
After action: a blameless postmortem is written within 5 business days, reviewed in a meeting, and its actions are tracked in Jira with owners and due dates. We focus on how the system allowed the failure, not on who was involved.
Training: IC training is held every quarter. Ask your manager to sign you up. After you have shadowed one incident, you can be IC.

sections.title: Product development process
sections.tags: product process, discovery, prd, design review, launch, beta, ga, feature flags, roadmap, launch tiers, customer advisory board, product management, release process, go to market
sections.body:
Stages of a product idea:
1. Discovery: the product manager and designer talk to at least 5 customers, review data and write a one-page problem statement.
2. Definition: a product requirements document (PRD) covering the problem, who it is for, success measures and what is out of scope. Engineering gives a rough effort estimate at this stage.
3. Design review: the design is reviewed by the squad, a peer designer and, for significant changes, customers.
4. Build: engineers deliver in small increments behind feature flags. The squad demos progress every week.
5. Beta: released to a small set of customers who opted in (the Customer Advisory Board and volunteers). We collect feedback for at least 2 weeks.
6. Launch: general availability (GA) with documentation, support training and sales enablement.
7. Review: 30 and 90 days after launch, the squad reviews whether the success measures were met.

Launch tiers decide how much effort goes into launching:
- Tier 1: major modules or changes, with a campaign, sales training and customer webinars.
- Tier 2: significant features, with a blog post, release notes and in-app announcement.
- Tier 3: small improvements, with release notes only.
Launch checklist: docs updated, support trained, sales enablement posted, pricing confirmed, legal and security review complete, rollback plan ready, and a status-page message drafted.
Roadmap: the roadmap is reviewed monthly and is shared internally. Dates in the roadmap are plans, not promises. Never share roadmap dates with customers unless Product has approved them for that customer.
Customer Advisory Board: 12 customers that meet quarterly with Product. Ask Customer Success if you think a customer should join.
Feedback: anyone can submit product feedback in #product-feedback. Product reviews every submission.

Approvals: everything that goes outside the company (blog posts, web pages, webinars, decks shown to customers, press releases, social ads) needs Marketing approval. Claims about security, compliance, performance or results also need Legal or the subject expert to review them. Allow 3 business days.

sections.title: Finance processes: close, budgets and headcount
sections.tags: month-end close, budget, forecast, headcount planning, accounts payable, invoicing, revenue recognition, vendor payments, finance calendar, annual planning, purchase order, net 30
sections.body:
Month-end close: Finance closes the books by business day 5 of each month. Expenses and receipts must be submitted in Ramp by the last business day of the month so they land in the right period. Sales and Customer Success confirm bookings and renewals by business day 2.
Invoicing customers: annual invoices are issued on the contract start date on net-30 terms. Finance follows up on overdue invoices at 15, 30 and 45 days. Do not promise customers credits or extended terms. Send requests to finance@meridianworks.example.
Paying vendors: approved invoices are paid every Thursday on net-30 terms. Send vendor invoices to ap@meridianworks.example, not to Finance staff directly. Vendor bank detail changes are verified by phone to prevent fraud. Never change payment details based on an email.
Budget cycle: annual planning runs from October to early December. Departments submit requests by mid-October, leadership reviews in November, and budgets are final by December 10. Mid-year re-forecast happens in June.
Headcount planning: headcount is approved once a year as part of the plan. New or backfill roles need VP and CFO approval before posting (see Manager handbook: hiring and interviewing).
Revenue recognition: subscription revenue is recognized evenly over the contract term. Finance handles it, so sales and support staff should not make side agreements that change terms.
Audit: we are audited each year. Keep records accurate and complete. If an auditor asks you for something, tell Finance and answer truthfully.
Segregation of duties: nobody approves their own spend. See Corporate cards, procurement and approvals.
Fraud and scams: be careful with urgent payment requests, even if they appear to come from an executive. Verify by calling the person. Report suspicious requests to finance@meridianworks.example and security@meridianworks.example.

Legal holds: if Legal tells you to preserve documents because of a dispute, do not delete anything (emails, chats, files) until Legal lifts the hold.
Subpoenas and government requests: if you receive one, do not respond. Send it to legal@meridianworks.example the same day.

sections.title: Code of conduct
sections.tags: code of conduct, conduct, behavior, respect, professional, expectations, rules, workplace behavior, ethics, bullying, integrity, honesty
sections.body:
Meridian Works is committed to a workplace where everyone is treated with respect. This code applies to everyone: employees, contractors, interns and leaders, at the office, remotely, at events, on business travel and online (including Slack, video calls and social events).

What we expect:
- Treat colleagues, customers and partners with courtesy and respect.
- Be honest. Do not lie, falsify records (including expenses and CRM data) or hide mistakes.
- Follow the law and company policy. If they seem to conflict, ask Legal.
- Protect customer and company information.
- Speak up when something seems wrong.

What is not acceptable: harassment, discrimination, bullying, threats or violence, retaliation against anyone who raises a concern, sharing offensive or sexually explicit material, being under the influence of alcohol or drugs while working (other than at approved events where alcohol is served in moderation), and theft or misuse of company property.

Speaking up: if you see or experience something concerning, you have several options (see Anti-harassment, reporting and investigations). Reporting in good faith is always safe, even if you turn out to be mistaken.
Consequences: violations may result in coaching, a written warning, suspension or termination, depending on the seriousness. Managers may face stricter consequences for failing to act on concerns they knew about.
Annual training: everyone completes Code of Conduct training within their first week and every year after.

sections.title: Anti-harassment, reporting and investigations
sections.tags: harassment, discrimination, report, retaliation, investigation, hotline, ethics hotline, complaint, hr complaint, misconduct, sexual harassment, hostile, whistleblower, anonymous report, how to report
sections.body:
We do not tolerate harassment or discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, genetic information or any other protected status. Harassment includes unwelcome comments, jokes, touching, messages, images and behavior that create an intimidating or hostile environment. It applies no matter the seniority of the people involved and no matter where it happens, including online and at social events.

How to report: you can use any of these. You do not need to go to your manager first.
- Talk to your manager, or any manager you trust.
- Contact People (HR): Priya Nair, people@meridianworks.example.
- Use the anonymous, independent Ethics Hotline: 1-800-555-0142 or meridianworks.ethicspoint.example, available 24/7.
- Contact the General Counsel, Wei Zhang, if your concern involves People or leadership.
Managers who hear a concern must pass it to People within 2 business days. They cannot decide to keep it private.

What happens next:
1. People acknowledges your report within 2 business days.
2. People speaks with you about what you would like to happen and about interim protections, such as changes to reporting lines or schedules.
3. A trained investigator, who is not connected to the people involved, gathers facts and speaks with those involved. Most investigations finish within 30 days. If it takes longer, you will be told.
4. You are told the outcome and whether action was taken. Details about discipline of others may be limited for privacy.

Confidentiality: reports are kept as confidential as possible. Information is shared only with those who need to know to investigate.
No retaliation: nobody may retaliate against you for making a report or taking part in an investigation in good faith. Retaliation is itself a serious violation. If you think it is happening, report it right away.
Whistleblowers: you may also report concerns about fraud, safety or legal violations. Nothing in this handbook stops you from reporting to a government agency.
Outside options: you can also contact the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) or your state agency. In the UK, contact ACAS. These are your rights, and we will not penalize you for using them.

sections.title: Ethics and conflicts of interest
sections.tags: conflict of interest, gifts, second job, moonlighting, outside work, board seat, bribery, kickback, related party, investing, side project, vendor gift, entertainment, anti-corruption
sections.body:
Conflicts of interest: a conflict exists when a personal interest could affect, or appear to affect, your judgment at work. Tell your manager and People before you do any of the following:
- Take a second job or paid side work (especially in our industry or for a customer, competitor or supplier).
- Serve on a board or advisory board.
- Invest in a competitor, customer or supplier (above a small holding in a publicly traded company).
- Hire, supervise or make pay decisions about a relative or a partner.
Most disclosed conflicts are fine with the right safeguards. Undisclosed ones are the problem.

Side projects: you may work on your own projects in your own time on your own equipment if they do not compete with Meridian Works, do not use company information or resources, and do not distract from your job. See Confidentiality, IP and outside activities.

Gifts and entertainment: you may accept a gift or meal from a vendor or customer worth up to $100 if it is occasional and not connected to a decision. Ask your manager before accepting anything more, and never accept cash or gift cards. Do not give gifts to customers above $100 without Finance approval. For government officials, do not give anything of value without Legal approval.
Bribery and corruption: never offer, promise or accept a bribe or kickback, in any form, anywhere in the world. This includes facilitation payments. We follow the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act and the UK Bribery Act.
Accurate records: books, expense reports, CRM entries and commission claims must be accurate. Falsifying them is grounds for termination, even if no money is involved.
Insider information: do not trade in a customer's or partner's securities using non-public information you learn through work.
If in doubt: ask Legal or People. It's always better to ask before you act.

sections.title: Security essentials
sections.tags: security, mfa, password, phishing, vpn, lost laptop, encryption, lock screen, clean desk, tailgating, byod, usb, public wifi, report phish, two-factor, authenticator
sections.body:
Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required on every account. Use the Okta Verify app or a hardware key. Do not share codes with anyone, including IT. IT will never ask for them.
Passwords: use 1Password. Passwords must be at least 14 characters and unique. Never reuse a password.
Lock your screen whenever you step away (Ctrl+Cmd+Q on a Mac). Use the company VPN on public Wi-Fi.
Device rules: company laptops are encrypted (FileVault) and managed by IT. Keep them updated (restart when asked). Do not disable security tools. Do not install unapproved software.
Personal devices: you may use your phone for Slack, email and Okta. Do not access or store customer data on personal computers or phones. Do not save work files to personal cloud storage.
Removable media: USB drives are blocked. Ask IT if you have a business need.

Phishing: if a message looks suspicious, don't click. Forward it to security@meridianworks.example or use the "Report phish" button in Gmail. We run phishing simulations. Failing one is not punished, but reporting real ones is celebrated. Warning signs: urgency, an unexpected request for money or gift cards, a slightly wrong sender address, and links that don't match.
Lost or stolen device: report it within 1 hour to #it-help or security@meridianworks.example. We can remotely lock and wipe it. Reporting fast is what matters, and you won't be in trouble.
Physical security: wear your badge, do not let people tailgate you through doors, escort visitors, clear your desk and don't leave sensitive papers on printers.
Travel: use a privacy screen in public, don't leave devices in cars or checked baggage, and ask IT about loaner devices for high-risk countries.
Training: Security Basics within your first week, then annually.

sections.title: Data classification and privacy
sections.tags: data classification, customer data, pii, gdpr, privacy, confidential, restricted, soc 2, retention, data handling, personal data, data subject, sharing data, compliance
sections.body:
Data classes:
- Public: approved marketing content, published documentation.
- Internal: most everyday company information (plans, internal docs). Do not share outside the company.
- Confidential: customer data, contracts, financial results, source code, personnel information. Share only with people who need it, using approved tools.
- Restricted: credentials and keys, security findings, payment data, health information, government IDs. Only named people, with logging.

Customer data: can only be stored in approved systems (Salesforce, our production databases and the customer support tool). Never put it in personal email, personal cloud storage or a spreadsheet on your desktop. Never paste it into a tool that is not approved (see AI and tools policy). When you need customer data for support or analysis, use the minimum needed and delete copies when done.
Personal data and privacy law: we handle personal data of our customers' staff, and in Europe and the UK we follow GDPR and the UK GDPR. If a customer or individual asks to see, correct or delete their data, forward the request to privacy@meridianworks.example straight away. Do not answer it yourself. There are legal deadlines.
Employee data: your own personal data is handled under our Employee Privacy Notice in Rippling.
Retention: keep records for the times set by the Records Retention Schedule in Notion. Do not delete anything under legal hold. Legal will tell you if one applies.
Compliance: we hold a SOC 2 Type II report and are audited every year. Customers often ask about it. Send them to Sales Engineering or security@meridianworks.example and never send the report yourself.
Reporting: if you think customer data was exposed, treat it as a security incident and report immediately (see Security incidents).

sections.title: Security incidents
sections.tags: breach, incident, data breach, phishing click, compromised, hacked, report incident, suspicious, malware, lost data, security incident, incident response, ransomware
sections.body:
A security incident is anything that may have exposed or damaged company or customer data or systems: a lost device, a clicked phishing link, a wrongly shared file, unusual account activity, or a suspected breach.

What to do:
1. Report it within 1 hour to security@meridianworks.example, or in #security-incident (or page Security through PagerDuty if it is urgent and outside business hours). Do not try to investigate or fix it alone.
2. Tell your manager.
3. If you clicked a phishing link or entered a password, change the password from a different device and tell Security straight away.
4. Leave devices as they are (do not wipe or delete). Security will tell you what to do.
5. Preserve messages and files that might be evidence.

You will not be punished for reporting an honest mistake quickly. Delay and concealment are the problems.

What happens next: Security assigns a severity and an incident lead, contains the problem, investigates, and, where required, notifies customers and regulators. Legal decides when notification is needed. Some laws require notice within 72 hours, so speed matters.
Do not talk about an incident: do not discuss it on social media or with customers, or the press, until Legal and Communications say so.
Learning: significant incidents get a blameless review, and lessons go into training.
Security team: Ines Duarte (Head of Security), security@meridianworks.example.

sections.title: AI and tools policy
sections.tags: ai, artificial intelligence, chatgpt, llm, ai tools, generative ai, copilot, prompts, approved tools, ai policy, customer data in ai, ai use, assistant
sections.body:
We encourage you to use AI tools to work faster and better, within these rules.

Approved tools: only the AI assistants on the approved list in Notion (currently our company AI workspace and the coding assistant licensed to Engineering). These have contracts that protect our data. New tools need a software request (see Equipment and IT support).

Never put any of the following into an AI tool that is not on the approved list:
- Customer data or anything that identifies a customer.
- Credentials, keys or tokens.
- Source code (unless the tool is the approved coding assistant).
- Unreleased financial results, board materials or acquisition plans.
- Personnel information or anything about a named colleague's performance, health or pay.
Even in approved tools, share only what you need.

Your responsibility: you are responsible for anything you send or publish, even if an AI tool wrote it. Check facts, numbers, names and links. Do not send AI-generated content to customers without reading it fully.
Disclosure: do not present AI-generated work as your own analysis when accuracy matters (for example a customer security questionnaire). Say where AI helped if someone asks.
Intellectual property: do not paste content you don't have the right to use (for example another company's confidential documents).
Code: AI-generated code goes through the same review, testing and security checks as any other code.
Interviews and hiring: do not use AI tools to make or recommend decisions about people (hiring, pay, promotion, discipline). People must decide.
Questions: ask #ai-help or security@meridianworks.example.

sections.title: Confidentiality, IP and outside activities

sections.body:
Confidentiality: you may not share non-public company or customer information outside the company, during or after your employment. This includes product plans, pricing, customer names (unless approved), source code, financial results and security details. Your confidentiality agreement is signed at hire.
Intellectual property: work you create for Meridian Works as part of your job, or using company time, equipment or information, belongs to the company (see your Confidentiality and Invention Assignment Agreement). Outside publications and speaking: submit any talk, article, podcast or panel that discusses Meridian Works, our customers or our industry work to Marketing at least 5 business days before. Speaking at conferences is encouraged. Marketing can help.
Non-competition: our employment agreements do not include non-compete clauses. You may take a job at a competitor when you leave, but you may not take confidential information, and you may not solicit our customers or employees in violation of your agreement. sections.title: Social media and media inquiries

sections.body:
Your personal social media is your own. You are free to talk about your work in general terms and to say that you work here. When you do, make it clear that you speak for yourself and not for the company.

sections.title: Employment basics and status
sections.tags: i-9, work authorization, at-will, background check, offer letter, employment agreement, employment status, full-time, part-time, contractor, intern, documents, eligibility to work, start paperwork, new hire paperwork
sections.body:
Offer letter: your offer letter states your role, level, manager, start date, pay, work location and whether you are exempt or non-exempt. If anything changes, People confirms it in writing.
At-will: employment at Meridian Works is at will in the US, which means either you or the company may end it at any time, with or without reason or notice, subject to the law. In the UK, your contract states your notice period.
Work authorization (I-9): US law requires us to verify your identity and right to work. Complete Section 1 of Form I-9 on or before your first day and show original documents to People within 3 business days of starting. Documents come from the government's approved list (for example a passport, or a driver's license with a Social Security card). You choose which to show. People cannot ask for specific documents. UK employees complete a right-to-work check.
Background checks: offers may be conditional on a background check, done with your consent and following fair-hiring laws. You have the right to a copy of the report and to dispute errors.
Employee types: full-time is 30 or more hours per week and eligible for the full benefits package. Part-time employees receive prorated PTO and are eligible for some benefits. Contractors are not employees and are managed by Finance rather than People. Interns are employees and follow this handbook.
Personal details: keep your address, emergency contacts and bank details current in Rippling. Emergency contacts are used only in emergencies.
Personnel files: kept confidential by People. You may ask to see your own file. Contact People.
Changes to this handbook: this handbook is updated regularly. People will announce significant changes in #general. It does not create a contract of employment.

sections.title: Performance concerns and discipline
sections.tags: discipline, warning, written warning, pip, termination, misconduct, progressive discipline, suspension, disciplinary process, performance plan, fired, dismissal
sections.body:
We aim to give people fair notice, clear expectations and real support before taking serious action.

Performance issues (not meeting expectations): your manager tells you in writing, explains what good looks like, agrees a plan with support and a timeline (typically a 30 to 60 day performance improvement plan, or PIP), and reviews progress weekly. You may ask People to attend meetings.
Conduct issues (breaking policy): depending on the seriousness, steps can include a coaching conversation, a written warning, a final warning, suspension with or without pay during an investigation, and termination.
Serious misconduct (for example harassment, violence, theft, falsifying records, or serious security or data breaches) can lead to immediate suspension or termination without earlier steps.

Fair process: you'll be told what the concern is, given a chance to respond, and People will review decisions before they're made. Decisions are documented.
Your rights: you may ask for a colleague to accompany you (in the UK, a colleague or trade union representative). You can appeal a formal written warning or a termination to the VP of People within 5 business days by email. The appeal is reviewed by someone who wasn't part of the original decision.
Retaliation: it is against policy to punish someone for raising a good-faith concern.
Confidentiality: discipline is confidential. Managers may not discuss it with the wider team.

sections.tags: resign, resignation, quit, notice, last day, offboarding, exit interview, final paycheck, cobra, 401k rollover, return equipment, layoff, severance, leaving, offboarding checklist, references
sections.body:
Notice: we ask for 2 weeks' notice when you resign, and longer for senior or customer-facing roles where possible. Tell your manager first, then submit your resignation in Rippling. Your manager and People will agree your last day.
Your last day: People sends you a checklist covering returning equipment, transferring your work, and turning off your accounts. Your accounts are closed at the end of your last day. Personal files should be removed beforehand.
Handover: write a handover doc in Notion covering what you own, where things are, and who to ask. Your manager reviews it with you.
Final pay: you receive your final paycheck by the next payday, or on your last day where state law requires it. This includes accrued unused PTO where required by state law (for example California).
Benefits: health coverage generally ends on the last day of the month you leave. You'll receive information about COBRA continuation coverage within 14 days. You can roll your 401(k) into another account or leave it. The company match is already vested. Your HSA is yours to keep.
Equity: you have 90 days from your last day to exercise vested options (see Compensation, levels and equity).
Equipment: return all company equipment within 7 days. Prepaid shipping boxes are provided to remote employees. Equipment not returned may be deducted from your final pay only where the law allows it.
Exit interview: offered to everyone. It is optional, and what you share can be anonymous. Feedback goes to People, not your manager.
References: employment verification (dates and title) is provided by People. Managers may give references in a personal capacity, but pay and performance details are not shared.
Layoffs or restructuring: if you are affected, you will be told in person (or by video) by your manager and People, and you will receive written information about severance, benefits, equity and support. Where the law requires advance notice, it is given.
Boomerangs: former employees who left in good standing are welcome to reapply.

sections.title: Acceptable use of company systems and monitoring
sections.tags: acceptable use, monitoring, privacy at work, personal use, email policy, internet use, company devices, surveillance, prohibited content, expectation of privacy, logging
sections.body:
Company systems (laptops, accounts, networks, Slack, email, cloud tools) are provided for work. Limited personal use is fine if it is occasional, does not slow your work, does not break any policy and does not use much bandwidth.

You must not use company systems to: access or share illegal, sexually explicit, hateful or harassing content; run a personal business; mine cryptocurrency; bypass security controls; install unapproved software; send mass messages that are not work-related; or gain access to data you are not authorized to see.
Accounts: your account is yours alone. Never share passwords, MFA codes or sessions.
Email and chat: messages on company systems belong to the company and may be retained. Write as if a customer or a colleague may read it. Do not use personal email or chat apps for work.
Monitoring notice: to protect security and comply with the law, the company logs activity on its systems, including sign-ins, file access, network traffic and device security status. The company may review messages or files on company systems where needed for a security investigation, a legal matter, a misconduct report or a legal obligation. Reviews are approved by Legal and People, are limited to what is necessary, and are not done for routine performance management.
What we do not monitor: we do not track keystrokes or screens as a routine matter, we do not turn on cameras or microphones on company laptops, and we do not monitor your personal devices or accounts.
Your privacy: we collect only what we need, keep it secure and limit access. See the Employee Privacy Notice in Rippling.
Reporting misuse: if you see a colleague misusing a system, tell your manager, People or Security. If you made a mistake, say so early.
Leaving: your access is removed at the end of your last day. Do not copy company files. Anything you need to keep (for example your pay stubs) should be downloaded in advance.

sections.title: Security program and audits
sections.tags: soc 2, penetration test, pen test, vulnerability management, bug bounty, security champions, vendor risk, audit, controls, patching, compliance program, iso, security questionnaire, disaster recovery
sections.body:
Our security program protects customer data and is verified by independent audits.

Certifications and audits: we hold a SOC 2 Type II report, audited each year. We undergo an independent penetration test every year and after major changes. Reports are shared with customers only under NDA and only through Sales Engineering or Security.
Vulnerability management: scanners run continuously. We fix vulnerabilities within these targets, measured from discovery: Critical 7 days, High 30 days, Medium 90 days. Engineers get tickets for their services, and overdue items are reported to leadership.
Bug bounty: we run a private bug bounty program for outside researchers. If someone reports a vulnerability to you (by email or social media), do not reply. Forward it to security@meridianworks.example the same day.
Security champions: each engineering squad has a champion who helps with design reviews and training. Volunteer by telling your manager.
Access control: least privilege and quarterly reviews (see Tools and access). Production access is logged and requires MFA.
Vendor risk: new vendors that touch data go through a security review. Approved vendors are reviewed again each year.
Change management: changes to production follow code review, testing and logged deployment. Emergency changes are reviewed afterwards.
Backups and recovery: customer data is backed up continuously, and restore tests are run every quarter. See Business continuity and disaster recovery.
Training and testing: Security Basics training, plus phishing simulations every quarter. Results are used to improve training, not to punish anyone.
Customer questions: customers often ask about our security. Direct them to the Trust Center page on our website, and send detailed questions to #security-reviews.
Reporting problems: security@meridianworks.example or #security-incident (see Security incidents).

sections.title: Business continuity and disaster recovery
sections.tags: business continuity, disaster recovery, bcp, dr, outage plan, backup, rto, rpo, emergency plan, office closed, failover, crisis, contingency
sections.body:
Goal: keep serving customers and protect people during a disruption, such as a cloud outage, a cyberattack, severe weather or a pandemic.

Service recovery targets for Meridian Flow:
- Recovery time objective (RTO): core services restored within 4 hours.
- Recovery point objective (RPO): no more than 15 minutes of data lost.
We keep the product running across multiple availability zones and keep backups in a second region. Failover is tested at least twice a year.

If an office is unavailable: everyone works from home. The Workplace team posts in #general and sends an alert by 6:30am local time. Non-exempt employees should work from home if they can, or tell their manager if they cannot.
If our systems are down: the incident process applies (see Incident commander guide). If Slack is down, use the backup channel, which is a group video bridge that is pinned in the Notion home page, and email.
Communication tree: in a major crisis, the executive team sets priorities. Department heads tell their teams. Managers call everyone on their team by phone within 2 hours if a crisis happens outside working hours. Keep your emergency contact details and your personal phone number in Rippling up to date. They are used only for emergencies.
People's safety: safety comes before work. If there is a threat to your safety (a storm, a fire, a security threat), look after yourself and your family first, and tell your manager when you can.
Testing: each year we run a tabletop exercise with leadership and a recovery test with Engineering. Employees may be invited to take part.
Your part: know where to find the plan in Notion, keep your contact details current, and keep your laptop charged and updated so you can work from anywhere.

sections.title: Accommodations and accessibility
sections.tags: accommodation, disability, reasonable adjustment, accessibility, pregnancy accommodation, ergonomic, lactation, religious accommodation, workplace adjustments, assistive technology, remote accommodations
sections.body:
We provide reasonable accommodations so that everyone can do their best work. You can ask at any time, and you never have to share a diagnosis with your manager.

Who can ask: anyone who needs a change to how they work because of a disability, a medical condition, pregnancy or recovery from childbirth, lactation, or a sincerely held religious belief.
Examples: a different desk or chair, assistive technology or software, a modified schedule, captions or interpreters, extra breaks, time off for treatment, working from home more often, or a different way to do a task. You don't need to use special words. Saying "I need some support with..." is enough.

How it works:
1. Tell People (people@meridianworks.example) or your manager. If you tell your manager, they will pass it to People without sharing details with others.
2. People meets you to understand what you need. They may ask for a note from a health provider only when it is necessary, and only about the need, not your full history.
3. Together you look at options. We aim to agree a plan within 10 business days, faster for urgent needs. Temporary arrangements can start right away.
4. The plan is reviewed after 30 days and then at least once a year, or whenever you want to change it.

Privacy: information about your medical condition is kept separate from your personnel file and shared only with people who need to know what adjustments to make. Your manager is told what you need, not why.
No retaliation: you will not be treated worse for asking for or using an accommodation.
Pregnancy and lactation: you may ask for adjustments during pregnancy and after childbirth, such as more frequent breaks, a stool, schedule changes or lifting restrictions. Lactation rooms are available in each office (see Offices and facilities).
Accessible tools: our internal tools should be accessible. If you find one that is not, report it in #it-help so it gets fixed.
Cost: the company pays for reasonable accommodations. You do not use your own stipend or learning budget.

sections.title: Employee surveys, feedback and the open door
sections.tags: engagement survey, feedback, suggestion, open door, anonymous questions, skip-level, ombudsperson, employee voice, pulse survey, concerns, speak up, how to give feedback to leadership
sections.body:
We want honest feedback about the company and we act on it.

Ways to give feedback:
- Quarterly engagement survey. It is anonymous. Results are shared with all employees within 3 weeks, with the actions leadership will take. Teams with fewer than 5 responses don't get their own results, to protect anonymity.
- All-hands questions. Submit questions in advance with the anonymous form, or ask live. Leadership answers every question, either in the meeting or in writing afterwards.
- Skip-level meetings. Each quarter you can book 30 minutes with your manager's manager.
- Office hours. Executive team members hold open office hours once a month. Find them in the Notion calendar.
- Direct to People. Contact people@meridianworks.example about anything. Conversations are confidential.
- Anonymous Ethics Hotline: 1-800-555-0142, for serious concerns.
- Suggestion box: #ideas is a Slack channel for ideas to improve the company. Product feedback goes to #product-feedback.

What we do with feedback: People summarizes themes for leadership each quarter. Leaders choose three actions and report progress at the following all-hands. Past changes that came from feedback: hybrid anchor days, no-meeting Wednesday afternoons, the $500 home-office stipend, and a longer secondary parental leave.
Ombudsperson: Helen Cho, VP of People, acts as a neutral contact if you have a concern you do not want to take to your manager or People. Discussions are confidential unless there is a safety or legal reason.
Giving feedback to your manager: your manager will ask for feedback in your 1:1. You can also give feedback in the review cycle. We do not punish people for honest, respectful feedback.
Responding to feedback you receive: listen, say thank you, and think before you respond. Ask questions to understand.

sections.title: Conferences, events and external engagement
sections.tags: conference, events, trade show, booth, speaking, sponsorship, external events, attend conference, industry events, swag, networking, travel for events
sections.body:
Attending a conference: get your manager's approval first, and explain what you will learn or what business purpose it serves. Use your learning budget for the registration (see Benefits: wellbeing, learning and perks). Book travel through Navan (see Travel policy). Share what you learned in a short Notion post or at a lunch-and-learn within 2 weeks of returning.
Working a booth: Marketing manages our events. Staff are chosen by managers and Marketing. Travel, lodging and meals are covered. You are representing the company, so keep to the code of conduct at all times, including after hours. Drink in moderation or not at all, and never when you are speaking to customers.
Meeting customers at events: log meetings in Salesforce within 48 hours. Do not give out pricing or roadmap dates that are not approved.
Speaking: submit talks to Marketing at least 5 business days before you confirm (see Confidentiality, IP and outside activities). Marketing can coach you and supply slides. Do not share customer names or confidential data in a talk.
Sponsorships and memberships: decided by Marketing and the CFO. Do not commit the company to anything.
Event safety: share your itinerary with your manager. If you feel unsafe or are subjected to inappropriate behavior at an event, leave, and tell your manager or People. You will be supported.
Customer events: we host a year-end customer event and several regional meetups. Staff attendance is planned by Customer Success and Sales.
Gifts and swag at events: you may accept small promotional items. See Ethics and conflicts of interest for gift limits.
Expenses: use Ramp. Per diems and hotel limits are in the Travel policy.
Family and partner guests: not covered by the company unless the event is explicitly for families.

sections.title: Quick reference: key numbers
sections.tags: cheat sheet, numbers, quick reference, limits, summary, key facts, deadlines, amounts, at a glance, how much, how many
sections.body:
Time off
- PTO: 20 days a year (carry over up to 5). Sick leave: 10 days. Company holidays: 11. Floating holidays: 2.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks (primary) and 8 weeks (secondary), 100% paid.
- Bereavement: 5 days (immediate family), 2 days (extended family).
- Volunteer days: 2 a year. Sabbatical: 4 weeks after 5 years.
- Request time off: 2 weeks ahead if longer than 3 days.

Money
- Payday: every other Friday. First paycheck: first payday after your second week.
- 401(k) match: 100% up to 4%, fully vested at once.
- HSA company contribution: $750 a year. Wellness stipend: $75 a month. Learning budget: $1,000 a year.
- Home-office stipend: $500 (claim within 90 days). Remote internet: up to $50 a month.
- Meal allowance on travel: $65 a day. Hotel cap: $250 a night ($325 in New York, San Francisco, London).
- Purchase limits: under $100 no pre-approval; $100 to $1,000 manager; over $1,000 manager and Finance.
- Gifts from vendors or customers: up to $100.
- Referral bonus: $2,000 ($3,000 for hard-to-fill Engineering roles).

Deadlines
- Benefits enrollment: 30 days from start date.
- Expense reports: 30 days (60 at the latest).
- Required training: end of your first week.
- Report a lost device: 1 hour. Report a security incident: 1 hour.
- Report a workplace injury: 24 hours.
- Life event changes to benefits: 30 days.
- Notice when you resign: 2 weeks.
- Return equipment after leaving: 7 days.
- Exercise vested options after leaving: 90 days.

Working
- Core hours: 10:00am to 3:00pm local. Office days (default): Tuesday to Thursday.
- All-hands: first Thursday of each month at 11:00am Central.
- Meetings: 25 or 50 minutes. No meetings on Wednesday afternoons.
- Slack replies: within one business day. IT: one business day (2 hours if blocked).
- Laptop refresh: every 3 years.

sections.title: New hire FAQ: pay, benefits and time off
sections.tags: faq, questions, common questions, new hire questions, how do i, can i, pay questions, benefits faq, time off faq
sections.body:
When will I get my first paycheck? On the first payday after your second week, and it may be partial. Set up direct deposit and tax forms in Rippling before then.
I haven't received my paycheck. What do I do? Check Rippling for a pay stub, then message People (people@meridianworks.example). Underpayments over $500 are corrected within 3 business days.
Can I take vacation in my first month? Yes. PTO accrues from day one, and you may take planned time off. Tell your manager early, ideally before you accept the offer if travel is booked.
How much notice do I need to give for time off? Two weeks for anything longer than 3 days. A few days off can be requested with less notice, but tell your manager as soon as you can.
Do I get paid when I'm sick? Yes. You get 10 paid sick days a year. No doctor's note is needed for absences shorter than 4 days.
What happens to my unused PTO at the end of the year? Up to 5 days carry over. Anything above that expires on December 31.
When does my health insurance start? The first day of the month after your start date. Enroll within 30 days of starting.
I missed the 30-day enrollment window. Can I still enroll? Only during open enrollment (November 2 to 13, 2026, effective January 1) or after a qualifying life event. People cannot make exceptions because the carrier sets the rules.
How do I add my spouse or child? Add them during enrollment or within 30 days of a qualifying event (marriage, birth, adoption, loss of other coverage). Upload documents in Rippling.
When can I start contributing to my 401(k)? After your first paycheck. You are not enrolled automatically. Choose your rate in Rippling. The company matches up to 4%.
Do I get a raise every year? Pay is reviewed every March, and changes take effect on April 1. A raise is not automatic. It depends on performance, level and market data.
How do I get reimbursed for something I bought? Submit it in Ramp with the receipt within 30 days. Reimbursements are paid within 10 business days of approval.
Can I use the learning budget for a conference? Yes, with your manager's approval. Travel to the conference is covered by the travel policy.
What's the difference between PTO and sick days? PTO is for vacation or personal time and requires advance notice. Sick leave is for illness, appointments and caring for family, and doesn't carry over.
Do I get my birthday off? There isn't a birthday holiday, but you can use one of your 2 floating holidays for it.
Who approves my time off? Your manager, usually within 2 business days.

sections.title: New hire FAQ: tools, access and technology
sections.tags: faq, it questions, tech faq, password reset, mfa, locked out, slack, laptop broken, software, vpn, how to access, tech support questions, forgot password
sections.body:
I'm locked out of my account. What do I do? Post in #it-help or email it@meridianworks.example. If you're blocked from working, say so, and IT responds within 2 hours. Never share your MFA code with anyone.
I forgot my password. Use the reset link in Okta. If you forgot your 1Password master password, contact IT because it can't be recovered without a reset.
My laptop is slow or broken. Post in #it-help. Do not try to repair it yourself. IT will replace it if needed.
How do I get access to a tool I need? Request it in Okta ("Request access") or in #it-help. Most requests are approved within one business day. Access to customer data also needs your manager's approval.
Can I install my own software? Only tools on the approved software list. Others need a software request reviewed by Security and Finance.
Can I use my personal phone for work? For Slack, email and Okta, yes. Do not store customer data or work files on personal devices.
How do I connect to the VPN? Use the company VPN client on public or unfamiliar Wi-Fi. Instructions are in Notion under IT.
I got a suspicious email. What do I do? Don't click. Report it using the "Report phish" button in Gmail or forward it to security@meridianworks.example.
I clicked a link and now I'm worried. Tell Security straight away (security@meridianworks.example or #security-incident). You will not be punished for reporting quickly.
Can I use AI tools for my work? Yes, the approved ones, and never with customer data or credentials. See the AI and tools policy.
Can I record a customer call? Only with the customer's clear consent. Use the approved recording tool.
How do I book a desk or meeting room? Use the Robin app. Book before you come in.
Where is the Wi-Fi password? You don't need one. Sign in to Meridian-Staff with Okta. Visitors use Meridian-Guest.
When do I get a new laptop? Every 3 years, or earlier if yours fails.
Where do I ask for a monitor or keyboard? The IT portal in Okta. Standard kit is one monitor, keyboard, mouse and headset.
I'm remote. Where should I ship my equipment when I leave? IT will send you a prepaid box. Return everything within 7 days.

sections.title: New hire FAQ: culture, etiquette and support
sections.tags: faq, culture questions, etiquette, dress code, working hours, manager, feedback, career, help, speak up, new hire tips, dumb question, feeling lost, overwhelmed
sections.body:
What's the dress code? There isn't a formal one. Dress comfortably and appropriately for what you're doing. If you're meeting customers in person, dress for them. Ask your manager if you're unsure.
What hours am I expected to work? Be reachable from 10:00am to 3:00pm in your local time. Otherwise your schedule is flexible, as long as your work gets done. Most people work about 40 hours a week.
Do I need to reply to Slack at night or on the weekend? No. Nobody is expected to. Use Do Not Disturb. For emergencies, the on-call system uses PagerDuty.
Is it okay to ask my manager a "dumb" question? Yes. Your first month is exactly when to ask. Your onboarding buddy is there for these too.
What if I don't get along with my manager? Try to talk to them first. If that doesn't work or you'd rather not, talk to People (people@meridianworks.example) or your manager's manager. You can also request a change of manager through People after 6 months. You don't need to put up with a bad situation.
What if I'm not sure I'm doing a good job? Ask your manager for direct feedback early and often. You'll have 30, 60 and 90-day check-ins. If you feel lost, say so. It's normal.
How do I give feedback about the company? Use the anonymous question form for the monthly all-hands, the quarterly engagement survey, or talk to People. Suggestions are welcome.
Can I move to a different team? After 12 months in a role you can apply for internal openings without your manager's permission. Before that, talk to your manager and People.
Who can I go to if I don't feel comfortable talking to my manager? People (Priya Nair, people@meridianworks.example), any manager you trust, or the anonymous Ethics Hotline (1-800-555-0142, 24/7).
What if something is wrong with my job or workplace and I'm not sure it's serious? Ask People. Asking a question doesn't start a formal process, and it stays confidential.
I'm feeling overwhelmed. What support is there? Talk to your manager about workload. The EAP offers 6 free confidential counseling sessions per issue for you and your household. If you are in crisis, call or text 988 (US).
Do people go out after work? Sometimes. There are monthly team socials and Wednesday team lunches. Everything is optional and alcohol-free options are always provided.
How do I get involved in things outside my team? Join an employee resource group, volunteer with your 2 paid days, come to lunch-and-learns, or join #social- channels.
Where can I find the company's goals? The company OKRs are in Notion and are presented at the start-of-quarter all-hands.

sections.title: Manager FAQ
sections.tags: manager faq, managers questions, how do i as a manager, approve time off, resignation, team problems, hr help for managers, manager help, frequently asked manager questions
sections.body:
Someone on my team told me about a personal problem. What do I do? Listen and be kind. Do not promise to keep it confidential if it is about harassment, safety or a legal issue. Point them to People and the EAP. Tell People yourself if you need to.
A team member resigned. What are the steps? Thank them, tell People, agree the last day (2 weeks is typical), plan the handover, and tell the team after the person has had a chance to tell the people closest to them. Do not try to change their mind in a way that puts pressure on them.
Can I approve someone's 3-week vacation? Usually yes, if the team can cover and the request was made at least 2 weeks ahead. If it affects a critical deadline, talk to them early.
Can I ask about someone's health when they are out sick? No. You can ask if they need anything, and when you can expect them back. Leave any medical details to them and People.
A team member's performance is slipping. When do I act? Act early. Give specific feedback, in writing, within a week or two. If there is no improvement, talk to People about a performance plan (PIP).
How do I handle a complaint about a colleague? Listen, take notes, do not investigate yourself, and pass it to People within 2 business days.
Can I give a raise to keep someone? Raises are decided in the pay review and promotion cycles, and must stay within the band. Off-cycle changes need People and Finance approval.
Who approves my team's expenses? You do, up to $1,000. Above that, Finance must approve too. You can never approve your own.
How do I get headcount for a new role? It needs to be in the annual plan, or approved by your VP and the CFO. See Manager handbook: hiring and interviewing.
Can I hire a friend or relative? Tell People first. You can't be the decision maker on hiring, pay or supervision of a relative or partner.
I think a team member is overworked. Ask about it in your 1:1, look at their workload, and adjust. Sustainable pace is one of our values.
How should I handle a team conflict? Talk to each person separately, then bring them together with a clear goal. People can help or mediate.
Where can I get help as a new manager? Your own manager, your People partner, the Managing at Meridian program and #managers.
